title: Kate Douglass Breaks Lilly King's US Open Record With 2:15.99 200 Breaststroke
content: At the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, Kate Douglass broke Lilly King's US Open Record in the women's 200m breaststroke with a time of 2:15.99 during the prelims. This performance improved upon King’s previous US Open Record of 2:17.03, set in 2019 at the ISL Final. Douglass, who holds the world record (2:12.50) and the World Cup record (2:12.72), was faster than King on the first three 50-meter splits, with the second 50 showing the largest gap—1.3 seconds faster. Douglass previously broke the world record at the 2024 SCM World Championships with a 2:12.50, following a prior record-breaking 2:12.72 during the 2023 World Cup Series. She also captured the LCM World title in the 200m breaststroke earlier that summer with a lifetime best of 2:18.50, the second-fastest time ever recorded. As the top-ranked female swimmer on the World Cup Series last year, Douglass is building momentum heading into the three-stop fall series.

title: Swimming World Cup: Pioggia Di Record Nella Seconda Serata Di Finali A Carmel
content: The second day of the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, became a celebration of speed, with four new records set—spanning world, American, and national records. Australian swimmer Mollie O'Callaghan set a new U.S. Open Record in the women’s 200-meter freestyle with a time of 1:50.77, surpassing Siobhan Haughey’s previous mark of 1:51.99 and becoming the third-fastest performer in history, behind only Haughey (1:50.31) and Sarah Sjöström (1:50.42). In the men’s 200-meter individual medley, Shaine Casas improved his own American and U.S. Open Record to 1:49.43, eight hundredths of a second faster than his time at the 2024 Short Course Worlds, and narrowly defeated Léon Marchand. Casas had already set a U.S. Open Record in the 100-meter individual medley the previous day (50.86), confirming his elite form. In the women’s 100-meter breaststroke, Germany’s Anna Elendt set a new national record of 1:03.83, improving her previous best of 1:04.05 from the 2022 World Championships. The gold went to American Kate Douglass (1:02.90), with Estonia’s Eneli Jefimova (1:03.35) second. Elendt now holds all German records in breaststroke (50, 100, and 200 meters) in both long and short course. In the men’s 50-meter breaststroke, Netherlands’ Caspar Corbeau set a new national record of 25.78, placing him among the top ten European performers of all time. He finished just three hundredths of a second behind South Africa’s Chris Smith (25.75), with Belarus’ Ilya Shymanovich third in 25.79, marking a high-level final. The event highlighted the depth of international swimming talent.

title: Anna Elendt Hits German Record of 1:03.83 In 100 Breaststroke
content: At the 2025 World Aquatics Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, Germany's Anna Elendt set a new German national record in the women's 100m breaststroke with a time of 1:03.83, earning bronze in the final. The event was held in short course meters (SCM) on October 12, 2025. American Kate Douglass won gold with a time of 1:02.90, while Estonia's Eneli Jefimova took silver in 1:03.35. Elendt, a 24-year-old former University of Texas swimmer, posted splits of 13.96, 16.40, 16.58, and 16.89. Her previous German national record was 1:04.05, set at the 2022 Short Course World Championships. The world record in the event stands at 1:02.36, jointly held by Alia Atkinson (Jamaica) and Ruta Meilutyte (Lithuania), with Meilutyte also holding the world junior and World Cup records. The U.S. Open record is 1:02.77, also held by Meilutyte.

title: World Cup Carmel Day 1: Swims You Might Have Missed (Records, Near Records, and New Races)
content: The first day of the 2025 World Aquatics Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, featured 12 events with notable performances, including an American Record and five U.S. Open Records. Rebecca Meder of South Africa narrowly missed the national and African record in the 200m breaststroke, finishing with a time of 2:18.14—just 0.12 seconds behind Tatjana Schoenmaker’s 2:18.02 record from 2020. Meder has significantly improved since 2022, when she swam 2:23.64, and her breaststroke split in the 200m IM at the 2025 World Championships improved to 37.56, ranking 7th among 16 semifinalists. Roos Vanotterdijk of Belgium set a new Belgian Record in the 100m IM with a time of 57.44, nearly half a second faster than her previous mark of 57.92. The 20-year-old sprint freestyler and backstroker showed increased front-end speed. Japanese 16-year-old Yumeki Kojima swam a best time of 1:53.61 in the 200m IM, finishing 7th, despite not being his primary event. Charlotte Crush, a 17-year-old from Louisville and the #1 recruit in the 2026 high school class, swam a 26.60 in the 50m backstroke, finishing 7th and improving by 0.04 seconds from prelims. This time ranks her 17th-fastest in American history, just behind Alex Walsh. All events were held in short course meters (25m).

title: Natation : record de Belgique et podium pour Roos Vanotterdijk sur 100m quatre nages en Coupe du monde en petit bassin
content: Roos Vanotterdijk secured third place in the 100m individual medley final at the first leg of the World Cup swimming series in short course (25m) pool in Carmel, Indiana, USA, clocking 57.44 seconds. This marked her second national record of the day, improving her previous Belgian record of 57.73 set earlier in the day during heats—19 hundredths of a second faster than the prior national mark set on December 15, 2024, in Copenhagen. She finished behind American swimmers Gretchen Walsh (55.91, best time of the year) and Kate Douglass (56.34). Vanotterdijk, 20 years old, also competed in the 100m backstroke heats earlier in the day, finishing ninth with a time of 26.73—22 hundredths faster than her previous Belgian record (26.51, set December 12, 2024, in Copenhagen), but did not qualify for the final. Florine Gaspard, 23, competed in the 100m individual medley heats (1:01.33, 19th), did not qualify for the final, but placed seventh in the 50m freestyle final with a time of 24.18 seconds—just behind Poland’s Katarzyna Wasick (23.29), Australia’s Alexandria Perkins (23.50), and Mollie O’Callaghan (23.96), the latter being the current national record holder in the 50m freestyle (23.99, set November 2, 2024, in Montpellier). Vanotterdijk is set to race in the heats of the 100m breaststroke, 50m butterfly, 100m butterfly, 100m freestyle, and 200m individual medley over the weekend. Gaspard will compete in the 100m breaststroke heats on Saturday (17:36 CET), and the 50m breaststroke and 100m freestyle heats on Sunday (17:00 and 17:30 CET). The World Cup short course series began in Carmel, Indiana, and will continue in Westmont, Illinois (October 17–19), and conclude in Toronto, Canada (October 23–25).

title: Gretchen Walsh Frantuma Il Record Del Mondo Nei 50 Farfalla Con 23.72
content: At the first stop of the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, American swimmer Gretchen Walsh set a new world record in the 50-meter butterfly with a time of 23.72 seconds, also breaking the World Cup record and the U.S. Open record. This performance followed her morning heat time of 24.13, which was the fastest in the preliminary rounds. In the final, Walsh dominated, finishing nearly one second ahead of her closest competitor. Australia’s Alex Perkins earned silver with a time of 24.64, while Belgium’s Roos Vanotterdijk claimed bronze with 25.44. Walsh’s new mark improves upon her previous world record of 23.94, set during the semifinals of the 2024 Short Course World Championships in Budapest, where she won gold in 24.01. She remains the only female swimmer in history to break the 24-second barrier in the 50-meter butterfly, cementing her status among the greatest sprinters in swimming history.

title: Kate Douglass Lowers Own US Open Record With 2:13.97 200 Breaststroke
content: At the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, Kate Douglass lowered her own US Open record in the 200-meter breaststroke with a time of 2:13.97 in the final, improving upon her previous US Open record of 2:17.03 set by Lilly King in 2019. In prelims earlier that day, Douglass swam a 2:15.99, which already broke the prior US Open record. She was faster on all four 50-meter splits in the final compared to prelims. Douglass, who holds the world record of 2:12.50 set at the 2024 SCM World Championships, was slightly slower on the second 100-meter leg compared to her world record swim. Her progression throughout the 2024–2025 World Cup season—improving from 2:15.96 in Shanghai to 2:14.16 in Incheon and 2:12.72 in Singapore—demonstrates consistent improvement, with her 2:12.72 previously being the World Cup record before she surpassed it at the World Championships. Her performance signals strong momentum heading into upcoming stops in Westmont, Illinois, and Toronto, Canada.

title: Max Morgan Breaks British Age Record On Opening 50 of 100 Breast
content: Max Morgan of Great Britain broke his own British Age Record in the 100 breaststroke event at the 2025 World Junior Swimming Championships, finishing third with a time of 27.41 in the opening 50 meters. This is the fifth time the record has been broken this summer, and Morgan's time is also under the 18-year-old British record of 27.58 set by Adam Peaty in 2013. Morgan's countrymate Filip Nowacki and World Junior Record holder Shin Ohashi finished ahead of him. Morgan will have three more chances to break the record in the 50 breaststroke event, which will be swum on day 5 of the meet.

title: Weltmeisterin Anna Elendt schwimmt deutschen Rekord
content: Swimming world champion Anna Elendt has broken a 16-year-old German record in the 200-meter breaststroke, clocking 2:20.22 minutes during the short-course World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, USA. This time surpasses the previous national record set by Caroline Ruhnau in 2009 by 0.19 seconds. Elendt now holds all six German records in breaststroke events on both 25-meter and 50-meter pools. The 24-year-old swimmer, who trains in the United States and represents SG Frankfurt, won the unexpected world title in the 100-meter breaststroke on the long course at the World Championships in Singapore in late July 2025. In the heats, Olympic champion Kate Douglass of the USA was the fastest with a time of 2:15.99 minutes.

title: 短池世界杯泳赛 美国泳将格雷琴再破50米蝶泳世界纪录
content: American swimmer Gretchen Walsh broke her own women's 50-meter butterfly short-course world record at the World Aquatics Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, on October 12, 2024, clocking 23.72 seconds—improving upon her previous record of 23.94 seconds set in December 2023 at the Short Course World Championships. This marks her 13th short-course world record overall, with 11 set at the December 2023 Short Course Worlds, including two in the 50m butterfly. She now holds the top five fastest times in the event's history. In the men's 200-meter individual medley, American Shaine Casas broke his own national record with a time of 1:49.43, defeating France’s Leon Marchand—world record holder and training partner—by 0.3 seconds. Marchand, who won four golds at the 2024 Paris Olympics and two individual medley titles at the 2024 Long Course World Championships, finished second with a time of 1:49.73, just shy of his own short-course world record of 1:48.88. The 2024 World Cup series is held entirely in North America, with upcoming stops in Westmont, Illinois, and Toronto, Canada. The overall champions for the season are Leon Marchand and American Kate Douglass, though Marchand is expected to skip the final two legs while Douglass plans to compete in all three. Canadian swimmer Summer McIntosh withdrew from the Carmel event due to illness but may still compete in Westmont and Toronto. The Carmel leg concluded on October 13, 2024, Singapore time.
